contract.words: Produce the strongest executable plan you can for collecting $10,000 in customer revenue within 30 days. Maximum total spending: $2,000. Maximum cumulative spending before proof of demand: $300 across all experiments and routes combined. Minimal owner involvement and no owner physical work. Do not use the owner's existing businesses or past campaign history as evidence.

strategy.title: Resell Textbroker-written SEO blog packages to US small businesses by cold email, gated by a USD 300 demand test
strategy.why: Ten USD 1,000 packages reach the USD 10,000 target; fulfilment is subcontracted to Textbroker so the owner does no work; buyers pay up front so receipts settle well inside 30 days. The price sits at or below the 2025 EFA work-for-hire blog median (25-45 cents/word, about USD 1,000-1,800 for 4,000 words). reviews.reasons: CONDITIONAL is not yet justified. A conditional plan must rest on an unknown only a live test measures (the close rate); this one leaves six links unestablished (demand, price, conversion, fulfilment, economics, settlement), several of which desk research decides before any money is spent: Textbroker publishes its own per-word client prices (so the $150/package cost and fulfilment are knowable now), and what US SMBs pay for outsourced SEO blog packages is published by agencies and marketplaces. The only price source cited (EFA work-for-hire blog rates) was rejected by Brain's evidence gate this hour on population and definitions, and every card fact is a RECOMMENDATION. Brain's planner reads NOT_VIABLE. The schedule is also not executable as written: brand-new sending domains cannot send 1,000 cold emails on day 1 without a warm-up, which pushes the day-10 proof later. Recomputed: 10 x $1,000 = $10,000; spend $150 + 10 x $150 = $1,650 (inside the $2,000 cap; pre-proof $150 inside the $300 cap), but the ledger omits card-processing fees (~3%, ~$300) and the cost of the scale-up sends the continue rule calls for.
findings: Price ($1,000/package) has no accepted evidence: the EFA claim was rejected (population: EFA members' clients, not US SMBs; definitions: per-word freelancer rates, not a content-mill package). At 25-45 cents/word x 4,000 words the EFA range is $1,000-1,800, so $1,000 is at its bottom edge, not 'below' it as the strategy says.
Textbroker cost and fulfilment are treated as live-test unknowns but are researchable now from Textbroker's published client prices; research them before calling the plan CONDITIONAL.

Cash ledger books all ten $1,000 receipts on day 10 (the proof day), while the validation says only 1 paid package is needed by day 10 and sends are scaled to 5,000 contacts afterwards; the COLLECT step is day 12 and settlement day 14. The receipts must be spread over the scale-up, and the ten closes need a stated close rate (10 paid of 1,000-5,000 cold contacts = 0.2-1%, at $1,000 paid up front) that is unevidenced.
New sending domains need warm-up before volume cold email; a day-1 send of 1,000 is not deliverable as planned, and the proof day should move accordingly (still inside 30 days?).

Ledger omits card-processor fees and the extra domains/list/Instantly costs of scaling to 5,000 contacts; maxExposure is $1,650 with no exposure cap, but the total spend must be shown inside $2,000 including those.
Executor capabilities SEND_A_MESSAGE/ISSUE_AN_INVOICE are NOT_CONNECTED and PAY_A_SUPPLIER is NOT_DECLARED; the plan should name how Brain gets each before day 1.
The Etsy alternative's exclusion arithmetic (about 360 orders at $28 = $10,080) is right; the excluded reason is reasonable.

conditions.why: The card's price is a RECOMMENDATION ($1,000) and the only revenueRange research was rejected by the gate; ten sales at an unevidenced price cannot carry the $10,000 target.
No EVIDENCE fact gives Textbroker's cost per package; the $150 figure and the $250 stop threshold rest on nothing yet, and they decide margin and total spend against the $2,000 cap.
Fulfilment by Textbroker is only a RECOMMENDATION; whether Textbroker 4-star writers deliver four 1,000-word SEO posts within the 5-day window is not established.

reviews.reasons: NO_PLAN is the right stance and it names the decisive gap correctly as missing evidence, not a false TARGET/CAPITAL constraint: neither card holds an EVIDENCE fact for price, buying signal or supplier cost (every fact is a RECOMMENDATION; the EFA price claim and the Etsy volume claim were both rejected by the gate on population/definitions), and Brain's planner independently reads NOT_VIABLE. The prior review's findings are answered one by one and the three conditions accepted. The experiment is inside every limit: $24 + $37 + $89 = $150 spent day 1, pre-proof $150 <= $300, total $150 <= $2,000, no owner physical work, no use of the owner's businesses or history. The 14-day warm-up is now planned and the consequence (proof day 22 leaves ~8 days for ~10 prepaid $1,000 packages) is stated honestly. No receipts are booked against unknowns. The owner can act on it: it is a bounded test, not a claimed route to $10,000.
findings: Factual error in the strategy: Textbroker does publish client prices — https://www.textbroker.com/clients-prices-conditions (opened 2026-11-27) states OpenOrder 'as little as 2.3 cents per word', TeamOrder 'starting at 3.5 cents/word', plus a $0.50 processing fee per order, commission included. Only /pricing 404s. The 4-star rate should be read from that page's pricing overview now (desk research, no spend), which makes ECONOMICS decidable before step t1 rather than a live-test unknown.

Brain's nextTest asks to discover and research further openings that can reach $10,000; the no-plan pursues only the one route whose proof lands on day 22. It should also commission discovery of openings with an existing buying signal that can settle inside 30 days, since this test cannot plausibly reach the target in the window even if it proves demand.
SEND_A_MESSAGE/READ_REPLIES remain NOT_CONNECTED; connecting the Instantly workspace on the new domains is a prerequisite of t1, as the answer says.
